results.summary_before: This project implements a shift register that loads a 6-bit input and shifts it out while encoding the bits for display. The write_not_shift control selects between loading and shifting, and the encoded bits are shown one at a time on an 8-segment display with the decimal point indicating the clock. It is tested using the standard Tiny Tapeout board with DIP switches for input and a display for output. The design is a simple demonstration of shift register and encoding logic.
results.summary: This project drives half of a P10 16x16 LED display module and initially displays the string TT03. It provides a 600 baud UART input to paint pixels, erase pixels, clear the display, and change the displayed color. Functionality is limited by resource availability and clock rate, with single color at once, no double buffer, and low refresh rate causing some flicker. A mode pin allows for two different clocking patterns, and external hardware includes an LED panel and a level converter to 5V logic.

results.summary_before: This design is a puzzle game that uses a 7-segment display and logic gates. The game logic is implemented with combinational and sequential logic. The design is intended for entertainment and educational purposes. It is a simple puzzle game implemented on a chip.
results.summary: This design is a simple tapped delay line with instrumentation. The continually changing data races through a chain of inverters and is sampled at different stages to become a digital signal. An edge detection circuit finds the rising edge, which is converted into a binary value, and a bank of flops samples eight sequential rising edge values. The UART is the only interface to the design, with commands for shift in, shift out, full sample, and scope.
